paragraphs.title: Jacob in the Land of Canaan

easy.question: Who lived in the land of Canaan?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Jacob dwelt.”

easy.question: In which land did Jacob live?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Jacob lived in “the land of Canaan.”

easy.question: What did Jacob do in the land?
easy.explanation: The word “dwelt” means that Jacob lived there.

medium.question: What does “the land where his father was a stranger” mean?
answers: The land where his father lived or stayed
The place where his father worked
The place where his father was buried
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the land where Jacob’s father had lived or stayed.

medium.question: What connection does the verse make between Canaan and the land of Jacob’s father?
answers: Canaan was the land where his father had lived
Jacob’s father did not know Canaan
medium.explanation: The verse describes the same place in two ways: his father’s land and Canaan.

medium.question: Why does the verse use two descriptions for Jacob’s home?
answers: To show both its family connection and its name
To say Jacob immediately moved elsewhere
To announce that Jacob left Canaan
medium.explanation: One description connects the land to Jacob’s father, and the other gives its name.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “the land where his father was a stranger”?
answers: The place had family significance for Jacob
challenge.explanation: Mentioning his father’s connection emphasizes the land’s family significance.

challenge.question: What is the language difference between “his father’s land” and “the land of Canaan”?
answers: The first describes the land by family connection; the second is its name
The first is a city and the second a person
The first describes time and the second an action
challenge.explanation: The first is a description involving his father, while the second is the place-name.

challenge.question: Which detail is not stated in the verse?
answers: The land was connected with his father’s residence
Why Jacob chose to live there
challenge.explanation: The verse says where Jacob lived and gives its connection to his father, but not why he chose it.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “the land where his father was a stranger”?
answers: The place had family significance for Jacob
questions.explanation: Mentioning his father’s connection emphasizes the land’s family significance.

questions.question: What is the language difference between “his father’s land” and “the land of Canaan”?
answers: The first describes the land by family connection; the second is its name
The first is a city and the second a person
The first describes time and the second an action
questions.explanation: The first is a description involving his father, while the second is the place-name.

questions.question: Which detail is not stated in the verse?
answers: The land was connected with his father’s residence
Why Jacob chose to live there
questions.explanation: The verse says where Jacob lived and gives its connection to his father, but not why he chose it.

paragraphs.title: Young Joseph and the Coat of Many Colors

easy.question: How old was Joseph when he fed the flock with his brothers?
easy.explanation: The verse says Joseph was seventeen years old.

easy.question: What did Israel make for Joseph?
easy.explanation: Israel loved Joseph more than his other children and made him a special coat.

easy.question: How did Joseph’s brothers feel toward him?
easy.explanation: Because their father loved Joseph more, they hated him.

medium.question: Why did Joseph’s brothers hate him?
answers: They saw that their father loved him more
Joseph did not feed the flock
Joseph was younger than they were
medium.explanation: The verse connects their hatred with their father’s special love for Joseph.

medium.question: What does “their evil report” mean in the verse?
answers: The bad things Joseph reported about them
medium.explanation: Joseph brought his father a bad report about his brothers.

medium.question: What happened first?
answers: The brothers could not speak peaceably to Joseph
medium.explanation: Israel made the coat before the verse describes the brothers’ hatred.

challenge.question: What can be inferred because the brothers “could not speak peaceably” to Joseph?
answers: They did not want to speak to him kindly
They did not know his language
challenge.explanation: Their hatred was so strong that they could not address Joseph peacefully.

challenge.question: Which detail especially shows Israel’s favoritism toward Joseph?
answers: Israel made him a coat of many colors
challenge.explanation: The special coat visibly showed Joseph’s favored position.

challenge.question: How are Joseph’s actions and his brothers’ response connected?
answers: Joseph reported bad things about them, while they hated him
Joseph praised them, so they honored him
Joseph avoided them, so they loved him
challenge.explanation: The verses place Joseph’s bad report beside the brothers’ hatred.

questions.question: What can be inferred because the brothers “could not speak peaceably” to Joseph?
answers: They did not want to speak to him kindly
They did not know his language
questions.explanation: Their hatred was so strong that they could not address Joseph peacefully.

questions.question: Which detail especially shows Israel’s favoritism toward Joseph?
answers: Israel made him a coat of many colors
questions.explanation: The special coat visibly showed Joseph’s favored position.

questions.question: How are Joseph’s actions and his brothers’ response connected?
answers: Joseph reported bad things about them, while they hated him
Joseph praised them, so they honored him
Joseph avoided them, so they loved him
questions.explanation: The verses place Joseph’s bad report beside the brothers’ hatred.

easy.question: What did Joseph do after he dreamed?
easy.explanation: Joseph dreamed and then told his brothers.

easy.question: What happened to the brothers’ hatred after Joseph told them the dream?
easy.explanation: The verse says they hated him even more.

easy.question: What did the brothers’ sheaves do in the dream?
easy.explanation: The brothers’ sheaves surrounded Joseph’s and bowed to it.

medium.question: Why did the dream make the brothers hate Joseph more?
answers: It suggested that Joseph would have authority over them
Joseph refused to work in the field
They did not understand it at all
medium.explanation: They understood the bowing sheaves as a sign that Joseph might rule them.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: The brothers asked, Joseph dreamed, then he told them
Joseph dreamed, told his brothers, and described the dream
Joseph described the dream, then dreamed it
medium.explanation: Joseph first dreamed, then told and described the dream.

medium.question: What are sheaves?
medium.explanation: A sheaf is a bundle of harvested grain stalks.

challenge.question: What can be learned from the difference between Joseph’s sheaf and the brothers’ sheaves?
answers: Joseph’s sheaf is central, while theirs bow to it
All the sheaves are presented as equal
challenge.explanation: Joseph’s sheaf stands upright while the others bow to it.

challenge.question: What does the brothers’ response, “Shalt thou indeed reign over us?” show?
answers: They were glad he would lead them
They understood the dream as predicting Joseph’s rule
They thought the dream concerned only fieldwork
challenge.explanation: They interpreted the bowing as a sign that Joseph would rule over them.

challenge.question: What does the repetition of “reign” and “have dominion” emphasize?
answers: The brothers were not speaking to Joseph
challenge.explanation: The repeated language focuses on the possibility of Joseph ruling them.

questions.question: What can be learned from the difference between Joseph’s sheaf and the brothers’ sheaves?
answers: Joseph’s sheaf is central, while theirs bow to it
All the sheaves are presented as equal
questions.explanation: Joseph’s sheaf stands upright while the others bow to it.

questions.question: What does the brothers’ response, “Shalt thou indeed reign over us?” show?
answers: They were glad he would lead them
They understood the dream as predicting Joseph’s rule
They thought the dream concerned only fieldwork
questions.explanation: They interpreted the bowing as a sign that Joseph would rule over them.

questions.question: What does the repetition of “reign” and “have dominion” emphasize?
answers: The brothers were not speaking to Joseph
questions.explanation: The repeated language focuses on the possibility of Joseph ruling them.

easy.question: What did Joseph see in his second dream?
answers: The sun, moon, and eleven stars bowing to him
His father and brothers eating together
easy.explanation: Joseph saw the sun, moon, and eleven stars bowing to him.

easy.question: To whom did Joseph first tell his second dream?
easy.explanation: Joseph told the dream to his brothers and then to his father.

easy.question: How did Joseph’s brothers respond to the dream?
easy.explanation: The verse says that his brothers envied him.

medium.question: Why did Jacob rebuke Joseph after hearing the dream?
answers: Joseph had not told his brothers
The dream suggested that his family would bow to Joseph
medium.explanation: Jacob understood the heavenly bodies as representing the family.

medium.question: What does “his father rebuked him” mean?
medium.explanation: To rebuke someone is to scold or correct him.

medium.question: How did Jacob’s response differ from the brothers’ response?
answers: Jacob envied him and the brothers rejoiced
Jacob rebuked Joseph and the brothers envied him
medium.explanation: Jacob rebuked Joseph, while the brothers envied him.

challenge.question: What can be inferred because Jacob rebuked Joseph but “observed the saying”?
answers: He rejected it openly but continued thinking about it
He agreed Joseph would rule the family
challenge.explanation: His rebuke showed objection, but he still kept the matter in mind.

challenge.question: Why were there eleven stars in the dream?
answers: That was the total number of Jacob’s children
There were only eleven stars in the sky
challenge.explanation: The eleven stars corresponded to Joseph’s eleven brothers.

challenge.question: What special meaning does it have that the sun, moon, and stars bowed to Joseph?
answers: The dream suggested Joseph would have higher status than his family
challenge.explanation: Bowing represents submission and points to Joseph’s future prominence.

questions.question: What can be inferred because Jacob rebuked Joseph but “observed the saying”?
answers: He rejected it openly but continued thinking about it
He agreed Joseph would rule the family
questions.explanation: His rebuke showed objection, but he still kept the matter in mind.

questions.question: Why were there eleven stars in the dream?
answers: That was the total number of Jacob’s children
There were only eleven stars in the sky
questions.explanation: The eleven stars corresponded to Joseph’s eleven brothers.

questions.question: What special meaning does it have that the sun, moon, and stars bowed to Joseph?
answers: The dream suggested Joseph would have higher status than his family
questions.explanation: Bowing represents submission and points to Joseph’s future prominence.

paragraphs.title: Joseph Is Sent to Find His Brothers

easy.question: Where did Joseph’s brothers go?
easy.explanation: The brothers went to feed their father’s flock in Shechem.

easy.question: Who sent Joseph to look for his brothers?
easy.explanation: Israel sent Joseph to see how his brothers and the flock were doing.

easy.question: Where did Joseph finally find his brothers?
easy.explanation: After learning they had gone to Dothan, Joseph found them there.

medium.question: Why did Joseph ask the man where his brothers were?
answers: He had not found them and was wandering
His father sent him to buy sheep
His brothers had sent him there
medium.explanation: Joseph was wandering in the field because he had not found his brothers.

medium.question: What did Joseph do after the man said they had gone to Dothan?
medium.explanation: Joseph went after them and found them in Dothan.

medium.question: What does “wandering in the field” mean?
medium.explanation: Joseph was searching for his brothers without knowing where they were.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Joseph asking, “Where do they feed their flocks?”
answers: He knew they had gone elsewhere
He still did not know where his brothers were
He had already found the flock
challenge.explanation: His question shows that he was still searching for them.

challenge.question: What was the order of the places Joseph passed?
answers: The vale of Hebron, Shechem, Dothan
challenge.explanation: Joseph was sent from Hebron, went to Shechem, and continued to Dothan.

challenge.question: What does Israel’s request to check both the brothers and the flock show?
answers: The flock mattered more than the brothers
Joseph was sent only to find pasture
The father wanted news of both his sons and his property
challenge.explanation: Israel wanted to know how both the brothers and the flock were doing.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Joseph asking, “Where do they feed their flocks?”
answers: He knew they had gone elsewhere
He still did not know where his brothers were
He had already found the flock
questions.explanation: His question shows that he was still searching for them.

questions.question: What was the order of the places Joseph passed?
answers: The vale of Hebron, Shechem, Dothan
questions.explanation: Joseph was sent from Hebron, went to Shechem, and continued to Dothan.

questions.question: What does Israel’s request to check both the brothers and the flock show?
answers: The flock mattered more than the brothers
Joseph was sent only to find pasture
The father wanted news of both his sons and his property
questions.explanation: Israel wanted to know how both the brothers and the flock were doing.

easy.question: Who saw Joseph from far away?
easy.explanation: The verse says that his brothers saw him from far away.

easy.question: What did the brothers first want to do to Joseph?
easy.explanation: They said, “Let us slay him.”

easy.question: Who tried to save Joseph?
easy.explanation: Reuben tried to deliver Joseph from his brothers.

medium.question: Why did the brothers plan to throw Joseph into a pit?
answers: To hide him and claim that a wild beast had eaten him
To teach him to care for the flock
To send him straight back to his father
medium.explanation: They planned to throw him into a pit and say that a beast had devoured him.

medium.question: What was Reuben’s plan after Joseph was thrown into the pit?
answers: To return him to his father
To leave him in the wilderness
medium.explanation: Reuben intended to rescue Joseph and return him to Jacob.

medium.question: What does “let us not kill him” mean in context?
answers: Let us not strike him dead
Let us not speak to him
Let us not search for him
medium.explanation: Reuben urged them not to kill Joseph.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the brothers calling Joseph “this dreamer”?
answers: They were happy to hear his dreams
They recognized him only by his clothing
They mocked him because of his dreams
challenge.explanation: The name was used while plotting against him and expressed hostility.

challenge.question: What was the main difference between the brothers’ plan and Reuben’s proposal?
answers: The brothers wanted Joseph dead, while Reuben wanted to prevent his death
The brothers wanted to return him, while Reuben wanted to sell him
The brothers wanted to hide him, while Reuben wanted to punish him
challenge.explanation: Reuben opposed killing Joseph and proposed the pit as a way to save him.

challenge.question: What does “before he came near unto them” show about the brothers?
answers: They spoke with him for a long time first
They decided to harm him before he reached them
They did not notice him until he was beside them
challenge.explanation: They plotted against Joseph before he even came close.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the brothers calling Joseph “this dreamer”?
answers: They were happy to hear his dreams
They recognized him only by his clothing
They mocked him because of his dreams
questions.explanation: The name was used while plotting against him and expressed hostility.

questions.question: What was the main difference between the brothers’ plan and Reuben’s proposal?
answers: The brothers wanted Joseph dead, while Reuben wanted to prevent his death
The brothers wanted to return him, while Reuben wanted to sell him
The brothers wanted to hide him, while Reuben wanted to punish him
questions.explanation: Reuben opposed killing Joseph and proposed the pit as a way to save him.

questions.question: What does “before he came near unto them” show about the brothers?
answers: They spoke with him for a long time first
They decided to harm him before he reached them
They did not notice him until he was beside them
questions.explanation: They plotted against Joseph before he even came close.

paragraphs.title: Joseph Is Thrown into the Pit

easy.question: What did the brothers do to Joseph when he reached them?
answers: They stripped him and his coat
easy.explanation: The brothers stripped Joseph of his coat.

easy.question: What kind of coat did Joseph wear?
easy.explanation: The verse calls it a coat of many colors.

easy.question: Where did the brothers throw Joseph?
easy.explanation: They cast Joseph into a pit.

medium.question: What was the order of the brothers’ actions?
answers: They stripped Joseph and then threw him into the pit
They threw him into the pit and then stripped him
They gave him water and dressed him
medium.explanation: They first stripped Joseph and then cast him into the pit.

medium.question: What does the empty pit show?
answers: The pit was full of food
medium.explanation: There was no water in the pit, so Joseph did not drown.

medium.question: What is a pit in this context?
medium.explanation: The verse describes a deep place with no water.

challenge.question: What can be inferred because “they stripped him” is plural?
answers: The pit was full of people
challenge.explanation: The plural verb shows that more than one person acted.

challenge.question: Why does the verse specifically mention Joseph’s coat of many colors?
answers: To emphasize the special garment he wore
To say the coat was wet
challenge.explanation: Mentioning its colors highlights the special coat.

challenge.question: Which phrase shows that the pit was not serving as a water source?
answers: “The pit was empty; there was no water in it”
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that there was no water in the pit.

questions.question: What can be inferred because “they stripped him” is plural?
answers: The pit was full of people
questions.explanation: The plural verb shows that more than one person acted.

questions.question: Why does the verse specifically mention Joseph’s coat of many colors?
answers: To emphasize the special garment he wore
To say the coat was wet
questions.explanation: Mentioning its colors highlights the special coat.

questions.question: Which phrase shows that the pit was not serving as a water source?
answers: “The pit was empty; there was no water in it”
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says that there was no water in the pit.

paragraphs.title: Joseph Is Sold to a Caravan

easy.question: Who saw the company of Ishmeelites?
easy.explanation: The brothers lifted their eyes and saw the approaching caravan.

easy.question: Where was Joseph brought?
easy.explanation: The verse says they brought Joseph into Egypt.

easy.question: For how much was Joseph sold?
easy.explanation: Joseph was sold for twenty pieces of silver.

medium.question: What did Judah suggest instead of killing Joseph?
medium.explanation: Judah proposed selling Joseph rather than killing him.

medium.question: What does “What profit is it?” mean here?
answers: What gain or benefit will there be?
medium.explanation: Judah asks what benefit they would get from killing Joseph.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Joseph was sold, then the brothers saw the caravan
The brothers killed Joseph, then the Midianites arrived
The brothers saw the caravan, Judah suggested selling Joseph, and Joseph was sold
medium.explanation: The caravan appeared first, Judah made his proposal, and Joseph was sold afterward.

challenge.question: What did Judah mean by saying, “He is our brother and our flesh”?
answers: He urged them not to kill Joseph directly
He wanted Joseph to rule them
He thought Joseph was not family
challenge.explanation: Judah appealed to their family relationship to prevent Joseph’s murder.

challenge.question: Who drew Joseph from the pit, and who bought him?
answers: The brothers drew him out, and Pharaoh bought him
The Midianites drew him out, and the Ishmeelites bought him
The Ishmeelites drew him out, and the Midianites bought him
challenge.explanation: The Midianite merchants drew Joseph out and sold him to the Ishmeelites.

challenge.question: What direction is indicated by “from Gilead” and “down to Egypt”?
answers: The caravan traveled from Egypt to Gilead
The caravan traveled from Gilead toward Egypt
challenge.explanation: The caravan came from Gilead and was heading down to Egypt.

questions.question: What did Judah mean by saying, “He is our brother and our flesh”?
answers: He urged them not to kill Joseph directly
He wanted Joseph to rule them
He thought Joseph was not family
questions.explanation: Judah appealed to their family relationship to prevent Joseph’s murder.

questions.question: Who drew Joseph from the pit, and who bought him?
answers: The brothers drew him out, and Pharaoh bought him
The Midianites drew him out, and the Ishmeelites bought him
The Ishmeelites drew him out, and the Midianites bought him
questions.explanation: The Midianite merchants drew Joseph out and sold him to the Ishmeelites.

questions.question: What direction is indicated by “from Gilead” and “down to Egypt”?
answers: The caravan traveled from Egypt to Gilead
The caravan traveled from Gilead toward Egypt
questions.explanation: The caravan came from Gilead and was heading down to Egypt.

paragraphs.title: Reuben Discovers That Joseph Is Gone

easy.question: Who returned to the pit?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Reuben returned to the pit.

easy.question: What did Reuben do when he saw that Joseph was not in the pit?
easy.explanation: Reuben tore his clothes in grief and alarm.

easy.question: What did Reuben say to his brothers?
answers: The child is not, and I, where shall I go?
easy.explanation: These are Reuben’s words after returning to the pit.

medium.question: Why did Reuben tear his clothes?
answers: Joseph was not in the pit
The brothers were angry with him
He had fallen into the pit
medium.explanation: He tore his clothes after discovering that Joseph was gone.

medium.question: What was the correct sequence of events?
answers: Reuben spoke to the brothers, returned to the pit, then tore his clothes
Reuben returned to the pit, saw Joseph was gone, tore his clothes, and went back to the brothers
Reuben tore his clothes, found Joseph, then returned to the pit
medium.explanation: That is the order described in the verses.

medium.question: What does “where shall I go?” express here?
answers: Where can I go or what can I do?
medium.explanation: Reuben expresses confusion and distress over Joseph’s disappearance.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that Reuben personally checked whether Joseph was in the pit?
answers: He returned to the pit and saw Joseph was gone
challenge.explanation: The verse says Reuben returned and saw that Joseph was not there.

challenge.question: What can be learned from Reuben calling Joseph “the child”?
answers: Joseph’s youth and vulnerability are emphasized
Joseph was older than his brothers
challenge.explanation: The term emphasizes that Joseph was young and defenseless.

challenge.question: What does “where shall I go?” express?
answers: A plan to reach a certain place
Panic and helplessness over Joseph’s disappearance
challenge.explanation: Reuben is distressed and does not know how to respond.

questions.question: Which detail shows that Reuben personally checked whether Joseph was in the pit?
answers: He returned to the pit and saw Joseph was gone
questions.explanation: The verse says Reuben returned and saw that Joseph was not there.

questions.question: What can be learned from Reuben calling Joseph “the child”?
answers: Joseph’s youth and vulnerability are emphasized
Joseph was older than his brothers
questions.explanation: The term emphasizes that Joseph was young and defenseless.

questions.question: What does “where shall I go?” express?
answers: A plan to reach a certain place
Panic and helplessness over Joseph’s disappearance
questions.explanation: Reuben is distressed and does not know how to respond.

paragraphs.title: Joseph’s Coat Is Dipped in Blood

easy.question: What did the brothers take?
easy.explanation: The verse says they took Joseph’s coat.

easy.question: What animal did they kill?
easy.explanation: They killed a kid of the goats.

easy.question: What did they do with Joseph’s coat?
easy.explanation: They dipped the coat in blood.

medium.question: Why did they kill a kid before dipping the coat?
medium.explanation: The slaughter provided the blood in which they dipped the coat.

medium.question: What does “dipped the coat in the blood” mean?
answers: They put it into the blood
medium.explanation: To dip something is to place it into a liquid.

medium.question: What is the order of events in the verse?
answers: They dipped the coat, took it, and killed a kid
They killed a kid, took the coat, and hid it
They took the coat, killed a kid, and dipped the coat in blood
medium.explanation: The verse gives that order.

challenge.question: What can be inferred because all the verbs are plural?
answers: The events happened at widely different times
challenge.explanation: The plural verbs show that several people participated.

challenge.question: Whose blood was used to dip the coat?
challenge.explanation: The blood came from the goat killed immediately beforehand.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the coat was a specific, known coat?
challenge.explanation: The definite article identifies a particular coat—Joseph’s.

questions.question: What can be inferred because all the verbs are plural?
answers: The events happened at widely different times
questions.explanation: The plural verbs show that several people participated.

questions.question: Whose blood was used to dip the coat?
questions.explanation: The blood came from the goat killed immediately beforehand.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the coat was a specific, known coat?
questions.explanation: The definite article identifies a particular coat—Joseph’s.

paragraphs.title: The Coat Is Shown to Jacob

easy.question: Who brought the coat of many colors to their father?
easy.explanation: The brothers brought the coat to their father.

easy.question: What did the brothers bring to their father?
easy.explanation: The verse specifically mentions the coat of many colors.

easy.question: What did the brothers ask their father to do?
answers: Identify whether it was his son’s coat
easy.explanation: They asked him to identify whether it belonged to his son.

medium.question: What is the order of events in the verse?
answers: They sent the coat, brought it to their father, and spoke to him
They spoke to their father, sewed the coat, and sent it
The father found the coat, then the brothers took it
medium.explanation: The brothers first sent and brought the coat, then spoke to their father.

medium.question: What can be understood from “This have we found”?
answers: They presented the coat as something they had found
They knew exactly who had worn it
They asked their father to find Joseph
medium.explanation: They described the coat as something found without explaining what happened to Joseph.

medium.question: What does “Know now” mean in “Know now whether it be thy son’s coat”?
answers: Identify and examine whether it is your son’s
medium.explanation: They asked their father to determine whether the coat belonged to his son.

challenge.question: What is notable about “whether it be thy son’s coat or no”?
answers: It states with certainty that Joseph died
It asks the father to decide whom the coat belonged to
It says the coat belonged to one of the brothers
challenge.explanation: The brothers did not state what happened; they left the conclusion to Jacob.

challenge.question: Which language detail shows that more than one person spoke to their father?
challenge.explanation: The plural wording shows that several people spoke.

challenge.question: Whom does “thy son” refer to?
answers: The son of the father they addressed
challenge.explanation: They were speaking to their father, so “thy son” means Joseph.

questions.question: What is notable about “whether it be thy son’s coat or no”?
answers: It states with certainty that Joseph died
It asks the father to decide whom the coat belonged to
It says the coat belonged to one of the brothers
questions.explanation: The brothers did not state what happened; they left the conclusion to Jacob.

questions.question: Which language detail shows that more than one person spoke to their father?
questions.explanation: The plural wording shows that several people spoke.

questions.question: Whom does “thy son” refer to?
answers: The son of the father they addressed
questions.explanation: They were speaking to their father, so “thy son” means Joseph.

paragraphs.title: Jacob Identifies the Coat and Mourns

easy.question: What did Jacob recognize?
easy.explanation: Jacob recognized the coat and called it his son’s coat.

easy.question: What did Jacob think had happened to Joseph?
answers: A wild beast had eaten him
easy.explanation: Jacob said that an evil beast had devoured him.

easy.question: How did Jacob show his grief?
answers: He tore his clothes and wore sackcloth
easy.explanation: Jacob tore his clothes and put sackcloth on his loins.

medium.question: What caused Jacob to think Joseph had been torn apart?
medium.explanation: Jacob drew the conclusion from the coat the brothers brought him.

medium.question: What does “mourned for his son” mean?
medium.explanation: Jacob remained in grief over his son.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: Jacob recognized the coat, tore his clothes, and mourned
Jacob mourned, recognized the coat, then tore his clothes
Jacob wore sackcloth, found Joseph, then recognized the coat
medium.explanation: Jacob first recognized the coat, then expressed his grief and mourned.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Jacob concluding Joseph was dead based on the coat?
answers: The brothers told him exactly what happened
The coat led him to conclude what happened without seeing it
challenge.explanation: Jacob inferred the event from the coat; he did not witness it.

challenge.question: What does wearing sackcloth together with tearing his clothes express?
answers: Deep mourning shown in both actions and clothing
challenge.explanation: Both actions visibly expressed Jacob’s deep grief.

challenge.question: What does “many days” emphasize?
answers: His mourning lasted a long time
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the duration of Jacob’s mourning.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Jacob concluding Joseph was dead based on the coat?
answers: The brothers told him exactly what happened
The coat led him to conclude what happened without seeing it
questions.explanation: Jacob inferred the event from the coat; he did not witness it.

questions.question: What does wearing sackcloth together with tearing his clothes express?
answers: Deep mourning shown in both actions and clothing
questions.explanation: Both actions visibly expressed Jacob’s deep grief.

questions.question: What does “many days” emphasize?
answers: His mourning lasted a long time
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the duration of Jacob’s mourning.

paragraphs.title: The Family Tries to Comfort Jacob

easy.question: Who rose to comfort Jacob?
easy.explanation: The verse says that all his sons and daughters rose to comfort him.

easy.question: How did Jacob respond to their attempts to comfort him?
easy.explanation: Jacob refused to be comforted.

easy.question: What did Joseph’s father do at the end of the verse?
easy.explanation: The verse says that his father wept for him.
